title: A message to another session that names a commit, record or PR that does not exist is caught
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1 sent runner 8 a record link it typed before the post returned, so the link pointed at nothing; it corrected it with a second message (coordinator, 02:12 CST Nov 8). Step agent-report-shas-resolve covers an agent's hand-back only, not send_message (that lane, 02:15 CST). INCIDENT 15:55 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 15:55, its own error; n=1 here): at 15:53 the coordinator sent the #3352 lane a --fix-check hash typed from memory past its first 12 characters; corrected 15:54 (copy the Head from the record comment). Coordinator's guard: a send that names a 40-character hash matching no ref or comment is refused (it asked for the slug message-hash-matches-ref). Triage filed it HERE, not as a new step: this step already covers a message that names a commit that does not exist (one record per question); the hash form (40 characters that match no ref or comment) is the case to add. If the coordinator wants a separate step, it says so. SECOND SAMPLE 16:36 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 16:34, its own mistake): in a batch of calls it typed a session id from memory into a send_message ("placeholder" text); the tool refused it as unverifiable and nothing was delivered. The tool's own verify worked, so no new guard is asked; the guard is this step. First sample: the 15:53 hash typed from memory.
note: Fix: the commit-hash part may reuse agent-report-shas-resolve's function as a second caller on mcp__claude-code-remote__send_message, with a rule for which repo a hash resolves against (lanes often send hashes from another repo, so the sender's cwd alone gives false alarms). A record link or PR number needs a GitHub read in a PreToolUse hook, a network call on every send: state that cost, or check only the commit-hash part. Red case first: a message with a made-up hash.
